article_title: A 20th Century Home in an 18th Century Church
brief_extract: We very soon started to attend services at the ancient Parish Church of St. George, which stood with its tower overlooking the Thames. It never seemed able to accommodate all its congregation so the Rector decided that a new aisle must be added.

brief_context: Area of Gravesend that saw a shift in population.
article_title: A 20th Century Home in an 18th Century Church
brief_extract:
I have many happy memories of those days. Owing to the shift of the population from the riverside, the congregation got less and less. there was much talk of the Church being demolished or

403

brief_context: Location of the Rector's lecture tour for fundraising.
brief_extract: moved to one of the recently built housing estates. Through the efforts of the Rector, and owing to the fact that Princess Pocahontas, an American national heroine, was buried in the Church in 1616, it was eventually agreed that it should not be demolished, but should cease to be the Parish Church, and become a Chapel of Unity and Pocahontas Memorial. Princess Pocahontas was the daughter of a Red Indian chief who opposed the landing of the Virginian colonists following Sir Walter Raleigh's voyage.

brief_context: Visited by Princess Pocahontas and Thomas Rolfe.
brief_extract: Princess Pocahontas was the daughter of a Red Indian chief who opposed the landing of the Virginian colonists following Sir Walter Raleigh's voyage. She saved the life of one Englishman, and as the wife of another, Thomas Rolfe, visited England, and was presented at Court. The first North American Christian, she died, aged 22, and the record of her burial is still to be seen in the old church register.

brief_context: Pocahontas was the first visitor from the New World.
brief_extract: The first North American Christian, she died, aged 22, and the record of her burial is still to be seen in the old church register. As the first visitor from the New World to Britain, she was the forerunner of the many thousands of Virginians who visit these shores, many of them making their way to Gravesend to the Chapel of Unity as they did on the 350th anniversary of the founding of the State of Virginia in 1956. After the closure of the Church, it was restored and redecorated, the money being raised by the Rector in a lecture tour of America.

brief_context: The country where the author is observing domestic life.
brief_extract: Though I had anticipated a very active attitude to automatic timing control on the electric cooker, very little interest was shown. all enthusiasm seemed to be centred on deep freezing, which is gradually playing a very important part in the domestic life of Sweden. Housewives are shown how the food can be prepared, and packed, by demonstrations and magazine articles, and a great deal of propaganda is made on this subject.

brief_context: Location of a hospital where a dietitian was interviewed.
brief_extract:
Just as we have spoken incessantly of television, which has not yet reached any great proportion in Sweden, so the Swedes discuss deep freezing. I talked with one of the chief dietitians from a large hospital in Stockholm who had been released from her post for one year to investigate the possibilities of extensive use of deep freeze foods in all hospitals. Practically every villa and farmhouse that I visited proudly displayed their "freeze-box" packed to capacity; they

were not so widely used in the towns, though many had the opportunity of renting a cubicle in the communal frozen locker at a small cost per year, and the waiting lists were long.

brief_context: Provided estimates on atomic energy contribution to agriculture
brief_extract: Radio-active materials are used in agricultural research, but hardly ever directly in farming. They reveal methods of fertilising the soil, developing insecticides and fungicides, and reducing pests; they can bring about genetic changes in plants to give desired types to withstand weather and disease, and the United States has estimated that the potential contribution of atomic energy to agriculture may be as great as the contribution of atomic energy to the generation of electric power. The Head of the Isotopes Division of the Atomic Energy Authority at Harwell has said: "I believe that this generation will see foods preserved by radiation only, that is, without refrigeration".

brief_context: Where Isabella Beeton was brought up.
brief_extract: Those who are acquainted with her famous tome, and even more those who are unacquainted with it, regard her as the very epitome of strait-laced Victorianism, a black-encased matron with many years of laying down the household law behind her. In reality Isabella Beeton was a very modern-minded girl, who was brought up in the Grand Stand of Epsom Racecourse, married at 20 a gay, talented publisher of mercurial temperament, travelled with him at breakneck speed in France and Germany, and who died at 28 in giving birth to her fourth child. Nancy Spain writes charmingly of the 28 closely-packed years of her step-great-aunt’s life, closely-packed for, until her marriage, Isabella had the care of twenty younger brothers and sisters, and on setting up her own household she produced her famous volume, with every recipe personally tested, and also took a large part in her husband’s publishing business.

brief_context: The place where Isabella and Sam established their life.
brief_extract: Nancy Spain gives a vivid and fully-documented picture of the relationship between Isabella and Sam, and her extracts from their letters are especially well chosen. It would be tempting to describe the crowded years of their married life, the establishment at Pinner, the trips to Paris to collect fashion plates, the holiday in Killarney intended as relaxation but full of observation, but that would be to detract from a book which will give pleasure and much-needed information to all. Having read the life of this amazing young woman, one can begin to understand how she was able at 26 to compile "The Book of Household Management", and one realises that it is based on experience but packed into a shorter lifetime than is accorded to most of us.

brief_extract:
Dream or Nightmare
Two recent exhibitions of home equipment illustrated the benefits and the drawbacks of automation in the home. In an exhibition in Paris the intimidating and soulless efficiency of the American "Kitchen of Tomorrow" indicated what can happen when planning is undertaken without regard to the housewife as a person. The mechanical equipment took away any pride of creation and gave her in return a guilty conscience if she did not match up to the machines!

Among other recent changes is the dissolution of the Electric Lamp Manufacturers' Association, and its replacement by the Electric Lamp Industry Council formed by a number of British firms whose lamp factories are licensed by the British Standards Institution. Progressive in what? For the woman in industry, electricity had indeed opened up possibilities of a good life, which would have appeared a wild dream during the years of the industrial revolution, not more than a hundred years ago—and even more wild in the grim period that preceded the industrial revolution when steam power had not been discovered and the cheapest

brief_context: Mentioned regarding the history of women in industry.
brief_extract: Dirt and women have always been sworn enemies. It was the unavoidable dirt of 19th century industry that made it inimical to educated women and so divorced them from the share they had had in planning the industries of the 17th and 18th centuries in Britain and reduced the share of women in industry to that of dull, heavy and ill-paid work that was done only by those who could gain their bread in no other way. Electricity had altered this grim picture of women at work.

brief_extract: A closer view reveals subtle differences, for there is a recurring pattern of trees for windbreaks to protect the farmsteads which are usually isolated; the cattle are kept within bounds by electric fences rather than by hedges; there are few dogs on the farms, and comparatively few cars on the roads. The interiors of the houses are very different in their open plan, their excellent heating system, and their pleasing decor in colour and design.

brief_context: Nation involved in a war with Denmark in 1864.
brief_extract:
At the same

THE OLD

time we began to appreciate something of the spirit of modern Denmark, which has produced a happy, balanced and hard-working people who have turned territorial loss into great material and spiritual gain. Perhaps it will be well to remind readers that after the war with Germany in 1864 when Denmark had to cede her southern provinces, Dalgas urged his fellowcountrymen to recompense themselves for the lost lands by intense cultivation and reclamation schemes. Thus, for instance, the busy port of Esbjerg now has a population of some 50,000, whereas at the beginning of the century there were less than a hundred people living on heath and marshland.

brief_context: The source country from which the factory was imported.
brief_extract:
This vast up-to-date works is one
of the wonders of the industrial
world. The new factory, which is
prefabricated, was imported from
Canada and is one-sixth of a mile
wide, and over one-third of a mile in
length. The preparation of the site
for the new building involved the ex-
cavation and dumping of 1½ million
cubic yards of chalk and main soil.

brief_context: The new factory's lighting installation is the largest in Europe.
brief_extract:
To supply steam and high pressure
hot water to the new building a new
boiler house has been erected which
is large enough to heat 5,000 homes. To provide ideal lighting condi-
tions, 66 miles of cable are con-
nected to 12,000 fluorescent fixtures:
this is the largest installation of this
type in Europe. Altogether, the
electricity requirements of this new
building will equal the normal de-
mand of a town of 30,000 inhabit-
ants.

THE ELECTRICAL AGE OCTOBER, 1957
ARCHITECTURE AND LIGHT
A Modern Conception at THE PORTLAND BUILDING,
NOTTINGHAM UNIVERSITY
By PHYLLIS THOMPSON
("Electrical Review")
NOTTINGHAM University is indeed fortunate in its site, in its architecture, and in its decor. While floodlighting can enhance the beauties of this imposing group of buildings set on a commanding site in parkland over-looking the Trent Valley, interior lighting provides aesthetic interest in a variety of ways, in which full use is made of new fabrics and of colours not traditionally used in an academic establishment. At the same time, the time-honoured materials, such as stone and wood, have been carefully chosen so that their intrinsic beauties are matched to the architectural setting to produce the required effect, whether it is the majestic appearance of a Renaissance Palace, both inside and out-side, the contemplative atmosphere of the beautiful Chapel and theological library, the gay and efficient service of the various cafeteria, or the blend of the dignified and the intimate in the several common rooms.

brief_context: A bookseller from the city runs the foyer bookshop.
brief_extract: The four main entrance doors are of bronze, each cast in one piece, and easily folded back. In the octagonal foyer is a bookshop run by a bookseller from the City, and this leads into a further vestibule, where the combination of light and colour is first presented in three grey-blue walls and one in rich terra-cotta colour with a pleasing contemporary centre fitting. The entrance to a gay coffee room is flanked by plants in "Festival Hall" style, and here the radiators are concealed by decorative chains.

WITH "Electricity for Everywoman" very much in mind we at headquarters have been getting some first-hand information about some of the many special uses of electricity which might come within the scope of our campaign. For the Disabled
The interest which our President, Lady Kilmuir, was taking in the meeting in London of the International Congress for the Welfare of Cripples led some of us to visit the exhibition which was organised in conjunction with the Congress. One of the objects of the exhibition was to demonstrate the various ways in which disabled people are helped to lead normal lives and what interested us most, naturally, was the Electrical Development Association's exhibit which illustrated the part that electricity can play in improving the life of handicapped persons, especially those living at home and caring for themselves.

brief_context: Facility visited to observe treatments for injured or paralysed limbs.
brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE OCTOBER, 1957

from a wheel chair. On the whole, however, it was a very ordinary kitchen with normal equipment, and an occupational therapist was able to demonstrate how simply and safely and with how little physical effort all the electrical appliances could be operated by someone sitting in an electrically controlled wheel chair, thus con- firming the title of the exhibit, "Electricity Lends a Hand to the Disabled."

Restoring to Service
Our conversation with the occupational therapist on the stand led to an invitation to visit the Medical Rehabilitation Centre where she worked, and we spent a most absorbing afternoon at the Centre seeing the various kinds of treatment given to the patients to enable them to regain the use of injured or paralysed limbs and muscles, or to cope with con- tinuing disablement. We did not have to look far to find the elec- trical interest.

Domestic Economy in Denmark
PLANNING in Denmark is an
example of the art which con-
ceals art, for as far as household
running is concerned gaiety and
efficiency go hand in hand. This is
largely due to the excellent system
of domestic economy training
which begins with the teen-ager
and, in a special University exten-
sion course, covers graduates even
up to the age of 60.

brief_context: Location of a domestic economy school visited by the writer.

A recent visit made by the
writer in company with Electrical

country emphasised many aspects
of Danish domestic economy, and
three establishments were of
special interest. Veilby Domestic Economy School
At Veilby in Eastern Jutland a
delightful whitewashed, red-tiled
house provided agricultural
courses for young men in winter
and two domestic economy
courses for girls at other times of
the year. For each course some
60 girls aged from 16 to 25 come
from all over Denmark, the early
course covering those with a more
elementary education, and the
later course comprising those
with a more advanced educa-
tion.

brief_context: Referenced in relation to a previously built electrical link.
brief_extract: One half of the 35 mile long cable will be manufactured in Britain, and one half in France. A convertor plant of very special design is being built by a Swedish company which successfully carried out the link between the Swedish mainland and the Island of Gotland, but the cable installation will be different, as one of the many technical problems in laying the cable is that of avoiding deviation of the magnetic compasses of ships passing over it. The whole project is a major experiment in new techniques in high voltage transfer, and much depends on the flexibility and reliability of the connection and on methods of co-ordination between the control centres in Britain and France.

article_title: Electrical Housecraft in Austria and Italy
brief_extract:
Electrical Housecraft in Austria and Italy
Miss Marion Binks, holder of the 13th Travelling Exhibition awarded by the Caroline Haslett Trust, is now visiting Austria and Italy to study aspects of electrical housecraft in these two countries. In Austria she will visit the Vienna Fair, and will see something of electricity in the life of the capital. She will also see supply in operation in town and country households in the Austrian Provinces, and visit testing houses, factories and institutions where large-scale equipment is used, as well as show houses and a Building Exhibition.

By MISS M. I.

brief_context: The branch to which the author belongs.
brief_extract: I. RALPHS, member of Bromsgrove Branch. As members approached the largest international airport in the world they were filled with an exhilerating sense of excitement.

location_standardised: Heathrow Airport, Hillingdon, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Area of London Airport visited by the members.
brief_extract: As members approached the largest international airport in the world they were filled with an exhilerating sense of excitement. The coach went quickly to the Central Terminal area through a half-mile tunnel which is air-conditioned and has fluorescent lighting. It is itself an important engineering feat, with runways and taxiways situated above and surrounding the central area.

location_standardised: Heathrow Airport, Hillingdon, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: A building at the airport providing various amenities.
brief_extract: The 127 feet high control tower is the nerve centre of the whole airport, where all air and ground traffic is controlled by radar, radio and other scientific means, electricity playing a vital part. Members entered the recently completed Queen's Building, which provides accommodation for airline staffs and many amenities for the public, such as a news cinema, exhibition hall, post office, and buffet and grill room. In the latter the tables are arranged in four tiers so that those taking a meal can also watch aircraft arriving.

brief_context: Location where approaching aircraft are directed to collect.
brief_extract: All incoming planes are supervised from 100 miles away to landing point, whilst aeroplanes taking off are guided until they reach the great air-lines. Approaching aircraft are directed to Epsom or Watford, where they collect under radio control and await their turn 1,000 feet above each other to land. Members also saw Calvert Approach lighting, an invaluable landing aid in poor visibility and at night.

brief_context: Mentioned in relation to Alcock and Brown's non-stop crossing.
brief_extract: A tremendous amount of electricity is used in both buildings. Members saw a striking memorial to Alcock and Brown, who made the first non-stop Atlantic crossing in 1919, and enjoyed a final view of the whole airport from the roof of the Queen's Building, which is designed as a series of spectacular gardens with terraces on five separate levels. A continuous microphone report on the landings and departures of all aircraft added further interest.

article_title: "WHY SHOULD EVERY BOY AND GIRL IN THIS MODERN AGE KNOW SOMETHING ABOUT ELECTRICITY?"
brief_extract:
The winning essays are published below. "WHY SHOULD EVERY BOY AND GIRL IN THIS MODERN AGE KNOW SOMETHING ABOUT ELECTRICITY?"
By JUDITH BIGGS of Marksbury Road Secondary School for Girls
(Age 14 years)
In these days, when we take electricity for granted, it is interesting to delve back into the past for a while, to find out about the beginning of it as a power. Among the ancient Greeks a man called Thales recorded the attraction of light bodies by a piece of amber and other things related to frictional electricity.
